topics.subject: Science (Physics)
core_principles: Distance is the total path length (scalar); Displacement is the shortest straight-line distance between initial and final positions (vector).
Average Speed = Total Distance / Total Time; Average Velocity = Total Displacement / Total Time.
Uniform acceleration equations: (1) v = u + at, (2) s = ut + 0.5*a*t^2, (3) v^2 = u^2 + 2as.
Slope of distance-time graph represents speed; Slope of velocity-time graph represents acceleration; Area under v-t graph represents displacement.
pitfalls: Displacement can be zero even if distance is positive (e.g. completing a circular lap).
Sign convention: Always treat deceleration (braking) as negative acceleration.

topics.subject: Science (Physics)
core_principles: Newton's First Law (Inertia): An object remains at rest or uniform motion unless acted upon by an unbalanced external force.
Newton's Second Law: Force is proportional to the rate of change of momentum: F = dp/dt = m*a.
Newton's Third Law: For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction acting on two different bodies.
Conservation of Momentum: In an isolated system, total momentum before collision = total momentum after collision: m1*u1 + m2*u2 = m1*v1 + m2*v2.
pitfalls: Action and reaction forces do NOT cancel each other because they act on different objects.

topics.subject: Science (Physics)
core_principles: Universal Law of Gravitation: Every particle attracts every other particle with force F = G * (m1*m2) / r^2, where G = 6.674e-11 N m^2/kg^2.
Acceleration due to gravity on Earth: g = G*M / R^2 ≈ 9.8 m/s^2.
Mass is constant everywhere; Weight W = m*g varies with gravitational field (zero at Earth's center).
Archimedes' Principle: An immersed body experiences an upward buoyant force equal to the weight of the fluid displaced: F_b = V_disp * rho_fluid * g.
pitfalls: Do not confuse universal constant G (scalar) with local acceleration g (vector).
Objects float when average density is less than liquid density.

topics.subject: Mathematics
core_principles: Remainder Theorem: When polynomial p(x) is divided by (x - a), the remainder is p(a).
Factor Theorem: (x - a) is a factor of p(x) if and only if p(a) = 0.
Standard algebraic identities: (a + b)^2 = a^2 + 2ab + b^2, (a - b)^2 = a^2 - 2ab + b^2, a^2 - b^2 = (a-b)(a+b), a^3 + b^3 = (a+b)(a^2 - ab + b^2).
pitfalls: Check if powers of variable x are whole numbers; negative or fractional exponents are not polynomials.

topics.subject: Science (Physics)
core_principles: Mirror Formula: 1/f = 1/v + 1/u, where u is object distance (always negative in Cartesian convention), v is image distance, f is focal length.
Lens Formula: 1/f = 1/v - 1/u.
Magnification: For mirrors m = -v/u = h_i/h_o; For lenses m = +v/u = h_i/h_o.
Snell's Law: n1 * sin(i) = n2 * sin(r) or n21 = sin(i)/sin(r).
Power of a Lens: P = 1 / f (in metres), measured in Dioptres (D). Convex lens has positive power; concave lens has negative power.
pitfalls: Always convert focal length to METRES before calculating power in Dioptres.
Remember the minus sign in mirror magnification (m = -v/u) vs lens (m = +v/u).

topics.subject: Science (Physics)
core_principles: Ohm's Law: Potential difference V across conductor is proportional to current I at constant temperature: V = I * R.
Resistance depends on length and area: R = rho * (L / A), where rho is resistivity.
Resistors in Series: R_eq = R1 + R2 + R3 (Current remains identical across each).
Resistors in Parallel: 1/R_eq = 1/R1 + 1/R2 + 1/R3 (Voltage remains identical across each).
Joule's Law of Heating: Heat H = I^2 * R * t.
Electric Power: P = V * I = I^2 * R = V^2 / R. Commercial unit: 1 kWh = 3.6e6 Joules.
pitfalls: Resistivity depends only on material and temperature, NOT on length or cross-sectional area.
In household wiring, appliances are always connected in PARALLEL so each receives full 220V.

topics.subject: Mathematics
core_principles: Right triangle ratios: sin(θ) = Opp/Hyp, cos(θ) = Adj/Hyp, tan(θ) = Opp/Adj.
Fundamental Identities: (1) sin^2(θ) + cos^2(θ) = 1, (2) 1 + tan^2(θ) = sec^2(θ), (3) 1 + cot^2(θ) = cosec^2(θ).
pitfalls: Check which angle is the reference angle: Opposite and Adjacent sides swap when looking from angle A versus angle C.

topics.subject: Mathematics
core_principles: Standard form: a*x^2 + b*x + c = 0 (where a ≠ 0).
Discriminant D = b^2 - 4*a*c governs root nature: D > 0 (two distinct real roots), D = 0 (two equal real roots), D < 0 (no real roots).
Quadratic Formula: x = (-b ± √(b^2 - 4ac)) / (2a).
pitfalls: Watch signs when calculating -b and b^2.

topics.subject: Physics
core_principles: Inclined plane: mg*sin(θ) parallel to incline, mg*cos(θ) perpendicular into incline.
Normal force N = mg*cos(θ); Kinetic friction f_k = μ_k * mg * cos(θ).
Net acceleration a = g*(sin(θ) - μ_k*cos(θ)).
Condition for motion on incline: tan(θ) > μ_s. If not, block remains at rest (a = 0).
pitfalls: Never blindly equate N = mg; normal force depends on component of weight and external perpendicular forces.

topics.subject: Mathematics
core_principles: Integration by Parts: ∫ u * v' dx = u * v - ∫ u' * v dx.
ILATE priority: Inverse trig > Logarithmic > Algebraic > Trigonometric > Exponential.
For ∫ x * sin(x) dx: u = x, dv = sin(x) dx => result = -x*cos(x) + sin(x) + C.
pitfalls: Do not forget integration constant + C.
formulas: \int u v' dx = u v - \int u' v dx
\int x \sin x \, dx = -x \cos x + \sin x + C

topics.subject: Chemistry
core_principles: For aA + bB ⇌ cC + dD: Kc = [C]^c * [D]^d / ([A]^a * [B]^b).
Kp = Kc * (R*T)^(Δn_g), where Δn_g = gaseous product moles - gaseous reactant moles.
Le Chatelier's Principle: System shifts to counteract perturbations in pressure, temperature, or concentration.
pitfalls: Solids and pure liquids are omitted from equilibrium expressions (activity = 1).
Temperature T must strictly be in Kelvin (K = °C + 273.15).
